title: Design Pinned LRU Cache
description:
Design an LRU cache `PinnedLRUCache` that supports pinning entries so they cannot be evicted:
- `PinnedLRUCache(int capacity)` initializes the cache with positive `capacity`.
- `int get(int key)` returns the value of `key` if present, otherwise `-1`. If `key` is present and currently **unpinned**, it is promoted to the most recently used (MRU) position.
- `boolean put(int key, int value)` inserts or updates `key` with `value`. If `key` already exists, update its value (and promote it to MRU if unpinned) and return `true`. If `key` does not exist and the cache is at `capacity`, evict the least recently used **unpinned** entry; if **all** entries are currently pinned (no entry can be evicted), leave the cache unchanged and return `false`. Otherwise insert `key` as an unpinned MRU entry and return `true`.
- `boolean pin(int key)` pins `key` (preventing eviction while still counting toward `capacity`) and returns `true` if `key` exists in the cache (even if already pinned), or `false` if `key` is absent.
- `boolean unpin(int key)` unpins `key` and returns `true` if `key` exists in the cache (if it was pinned, place it at the MRU position among unpinned entries), or `false` if `key` is absent.

All operations must run in `O(1)` time.
constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made to get, put, pin, and unpin.
hints: Maintain a hash map `key -> Node` for all cached entries (both pinned and unpinned) and a doubly linked list containing **only** the unpinned entries in MRU-to-LRU order.

`pin(key)` simply unlinks the node from the unpinned DLL (marking `pinned = true`), while `unpin(key)` marks `pinned = false` and inserts it at the head (MRU) of the unpinned DLL; eviction on `put` checks whether the unpinned DLL is empty.

examples.explanation: Key 1 is pinned so put(3, 30) evicts unpinned key 2 instead of key 1; pinning key 3 makes the cache full of pinned entries so put(4, 40) returns false.
Unpinning key 1 puts it at MRU ahead of key 2, so put(3, 30) evicts key 2 instead of key 1.
Pinning or unpinning a missing key returns false; updating an existing pinned key still succeeds and returns true.
